bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /images handler accepts request.query.src and passes it to imageProcessor. For any value beginning with http:// or https://, imageProcessor treats it as external, skips all local-path validation, and calls fetch(src) without a destination allowlist or network-address restriction. An attacker can therefore make the EverShop server request attacker-selected external or internal HTTP(S) resources, including link-local metadata services, producing blind SSRF.
flaw_origin: Commit 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 created both the front-store images handler and imageProcessor.ts. Its newly written external-URL branch classified a URL only by its http/https prefix and then directly executed fetch(src); the validation in the same function applied only to non-external filesystem paths. This is the first repository commit that contains both the public request path and the flawed server-side fetch mechanism, not a later move, refactor, revert, or release aggregate.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 shows human author and committer The Nguyen <6950941+treoden@users.noreply.github.com>, one parent, and the message 'Feat: Image component' with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other trailer/commit-object AI marker.
evidence: The assigned GHSA describes unauthenticated blind SSRF through GET /images?src=... in @evershop/evershop <=2.1.0 and records no first_patched_version. Its referenced researcher analysis identifies packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts and the direct fetch(src) call; public issue https://github.com/evershopcommerce/evershop/issues/928 independently gives the concrete metadata request GET /images?src=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ and calls the endpoint public.

At tag v2.1.0, packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/pages/frontStore/images/images.ts reads request.query.src and passes it to imageProcessor. In packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts, lines 74-75 recognize only the http/https prefix, lines 177-204 enter the external branch and call fetch(src), and lines 210-211 consume the response body. The local-path restrictions are confined to the !isExternalUrl branch.

git log -L 202,211:packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts v2.1.0 follows the vulnerable fetch block directly to new-file commit 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143. git blame -L 74,77 -L 177,211 v2.1.0 attributes the classifier and entire external-fetch block to the same commit. git log --all -S'const response = await fetch(src)' for that path returns only its addition in 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 and removal in fix af6e6fd935c4194668b11a924b847542598941f7.

git show 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 shows both packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/pages/frontStore/images/images.ts and packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts added from /dev/null. The commit is an ordinary single-parent commit whose direct parent is 753e8aeac5e7a9753731a8ad0f449c05cb2fa61e; no member/squash series is exposed to decompose.

Direct parent-tree verification: git cat-file -e 753e8aeac5e7a9753731a8ad0f449c05cb2fa61e:packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts fails because the path is absent, and the identical check for packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/pages/frontStore/images/images.ts also fails. Thus neither the vulnerable fetch implementation nor its /images request handler exists in the immediate parent.

Version boundary: git merge-base --is-ancestor 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 v2.0.1 exits 1, while git tag --contains 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 lists v2.1.0, v2.1.1, v2.1.2, and v2.2.1. The BIC therefore lands after v2.0.1 and before the advisory's affected v2.1.0 release. The later v2.1.1 and v2.1.2 tags also retain the vulnerable history, consistent with the advisory having no patched version and not being updated for later releases.

Fix lifecycle: the immediate parent b6333774b58359c806683c3135efba41af20cd69 of af6e6fd935c4194668b11a924b847542598941f7 still contains const response = await fetch(src). The fix commit adds packages/evershop/src/lib/util/secureFetch.ts with a default-deny IMAGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS allowlist, http/https parsing, and a guarded undici connector for every connection/redirect, then replaces fetch(src) with secureFetch(src) in imageProcessor.ts. This directly removes arbitrary-destination fetching for untrusted src values.

Patched boundary in available Git history: af6e6fd935c4194668b11a924b847542598941f7 is not an ancestor of tag v2.1.2 (git merge-base --is-ancestor exits 1); git tag --contains af6e6fd935c4194668b11a924b847542598941f7 lists v2.2.1, whose annotated tag resolves to commit 89d09fbd200931daa892c59ee8e5866490788e4c. Although the fix tree declares package version 2.1.3 and issue #928 has milestone v2.1.3, no v2.1.3 repository tag exists; v2.2.1 is the first available tag proven to contain the fix.

BIC-only AI check: the raw object for 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 has tree d3cc0f74005f428aabc43f863044a80ebec21881, parent 753e8aeac5e7a9753731a8ad0f449c05cb2fa61e, identical human author/committer The Nguyen, and only the subject 'Feat: Image component'. There are no trailers and no bot or AI identity. No later issue, branch, PR, refactor, or fix metadata was used to attribute the BIC.
reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle begins in 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143: the same commit creates the unauthenticated front-store /images handler and creates imageProcessor with an external-URL path that bypasses local checks and feeds attacker-controlled src directly to server-side fetch. Line history and the -S transition identify that commit as the smallest real first writer, and direct parent-tree checks prove both relevant files absent from 753e8aeac5e7a9753731a8ad0f449c05cb2fa61e. The BIC is present in v2.1.0 but absent from v2.0.1, matching the advisory's stated affected boundary; later v2.1.x tags remained vulnerable because the advisory had no patched release. Commit af6e6fd935c4194668b11a924b847542598941f7 is the direct fix because its parent still performs fetch(src) and its diff changes that exact sink to a default-deny allowlisted secureFetch; v2.2.1 is the first available tag containing it. Finally, the BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker or trailer. Under the required commit-object-only attribution rule, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
